speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are concerned about your husband's bizarre and agitated behavior; to help him, I need to ask you a few questions about his recent health and history. How long has he been exhibiting these symptoms, and have there been any recent changes in his diet, sleep, or medication use?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Delusional Disorder, Persecutory Type (or early Schizophrenia).

The patient's belief that he is being spied on and controlled by the NSA represents a fixed false belief (delusion) of persecution and control, which is not due to a primary mood disorder given the duration of the bizarre behaviors (6 weeks) and the specific nature of the delusion. His withdrawal, depression, and job termination are secondary to the onset of these psychotic symptoms. Have you noticed any hallucinations, such as hearing voices telling him what to do or seeing things that others don't?
